units.text: Trunk eclector traps (covering an area of approximately 0.2 m 2 ) were used to collect beetles emerging from the wood, while window traps (perspex pane: 10 · 15 cm, attached directly to the logs) were used to collect beetles attracted to or flying close to the logs (see Johansson et al. (2006) for further details about the traps). We restricted ourselves to sampling from our experimental logs in order to maintain the experimental aspect of this study. The species on which we focussed were found in substantial numbers in the substrates we examined, so substrate preference in the context of coarse woody debris is relevant for these species, although it probably does not cover all possible habitats for all species. Trapping was conducted over five time periods: July–August 2002; September 2002–May 2003; May–June 2003; June–July 2003; and July–September 2003. Window traps were used in all periods, except September 2002–May 2003 and July–September 2003. Samples collected from one additional nearby locality (also including a nature reserve, mature managed forest and clear-cut stand) using similar methods in four trapping periods in 2001 were also used for the morphological comparisons.

This correction allowed us to rule out the possibility that red-listed species could be found to be more site- or habitat-specific, simply as a result of random sampling. The hypotheses that redlisted species were found: (a) at fewer sites and (b) in fewer stand types and substrates than non-red-listed species were tested using a Chi-square test. Expected frequencies were the average of the frequencies for related non-red-listed species.
Fig. 1 – Mean ± SE aspect ratio for: (a) Epuraea, and (b) Tachinus. Red-listed species are shown with black bars.

Fig. 2 – Mean ± SE wing area for: (a) Epuraea (Ea = E. angustula; Eb = E. boreella; Ed = E. deubeli; El = E. longipennis; Ep = E. pygmaea), and (b) Tachinus (Te = T. elegans; Tl = T. laticollis; Tpa = T. palliatus; Tpr = T. proximus). Regression lines are for all individuals in all species. Symbols above the line have a lower wing loading than expected, based on their weight, while symbols below the line have a greater wing loading than expected. Black symbols represent red-listed species.
